items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: It wasn't Mason, was it? No, no, not Norman Mason.

ctx.x: Just a week ago tomorrow, we had a little interview with him out of his restaurant. Yeah.

Then we were, we were sorry to see, man, because we had a lot of fun on the boat. But we got soon tired of that food, man, we used to go out and buy sodas and stuff, we would eat that food. On the boat, yeah. See, we had one guy that we got out of, could eat all that food, one guy from, from, from Trigold Boy, we got from Ron Tibbetts, what was his name, climate player, Satchmo player, used to eat so much, remember he got drunk, he used to beat him, Sidney used to beat him with his hat. That quiet kid. What was…
Not Walter Thomas? No, no, not Walter. Walter was a good full of it, too. He died, you know.

items.title: Norman Mason Interview, 1960-02-06
items.q: in that group uh we had uh uh George Foster uh George Foster uh a New Orleans bass player

ctx.x: is Norman Kellogg Mason and my name is Paul Crawford and this is being recorded in the Sheraton Jefferson Hotel room 1153 in st. Louis Missouri and the date is February 6 1960 I believe that's right isn't it now mr. Mason would you tell us where you were born and when and what your parents

I was born in Nassau in the Bahama Islands November 25th in 1895 and my father's name was Ellis Mason Ellis and Alice yes and I came to the States in 1913 it was I first thought it was first said that I was born in Miami and went in Nassau but after a little more deliberation I find out that instead of it being that way I was really born in in Nassau started my father started me out playing the trumpet with intention of playing in the church which we were all members of the Episcopal Church but after a short time…
